# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling first** — before writing anything, have your top 3 coaches list every variation they're currently offering (class types, PT packages, nutrition add-ons, challenges). You'll spot inconsistencies, pricing gaps, and upsells you're leaving on the table.

• **Create two separate documents, not one** — coaches need a *delivery specification sheet* (class formats, duration, equipment needed, progression paths), while members need a *benefits-focused menu* (what results they get, what's included in each tier, why they'd pick option A vs B). These serve completely different purposes.

• **Price it strategically around your top performer** — identify your highest-revenue package or class format, then build the menu backward from that. Make it the "flagship" option coaches naturally recommend. Everything else anchors around it (cheaper entry-level, premium add-ons above).

• **Include a "what's NOT included" section** — ambiguity kills conversions. Explicitly state if PT clients can drop into group classes, if nutrition coaching requires gym membership, if challenges have extra fees. Removes objections before they surface.

• **Get coaches to validate it within 48 hours** — send drafts to your coaches asking "Can you confidently sell this?" and "What questions will members ask?" Their real-world pushback beats guessing every time.

Done right, this becomes your conversion tool AND your team's sales script.

**Insights**

1. **You've cracked the model in July—August confirms it's repeatable.** July's 215 leads at £2/lead with 29 sales (13.5% close) proved the offer and audience work. August halved spend but kept the unit economics intact: 50 leads at £3/lead, 23 sales (46% close rate). That 46% August close rate is an anomaly (possibly smaller, warmer lead pool or reporting lag), but the £3 CPL is your new baseline and it's profitable.

2. **April–June was a wasteland because you were either targeting wrong, using weak creative, or the offer hadn't landed.** Your CPL climbed from £6 to £21 as you burned cash chasing unqualified leads. July's 10x improvement in lead quality wasn't luck—something fundamental changed (audience, creative, landing page, offer messaging, or all of it).

3. **August's spend cliff (72% down from July) is leaving money on the table.** At £3 CPL and even a conservative 15% close rate (below July's 13.5%, above August's anomaly), you'd generate ~£1.80 profit per lead. You throttled budget when you should've been pouring it on.

---

**Actions**

1. **Immediately scale August's winning setup to £600–800/month.** You have proof of concept. Replicate the exact July/August audience segment, creative, and landing page. If 50 leads at £3 CPL × 15% close = 7.5 sales, that's £57 profit per month on an extra £400 spend. Test spend increases of +50% week-on-week and monitor CPL and CPC daily to catch decay early.

2. **Audit what changed between June and July.** Document the audience parameters, ad creative (headline, image, copy), landing page, offer, and call-to-action used in July. This is your control. You need this written down so you're not guessing next month. If you've already changed creative in August, pause and A/B test the old July version against new variants—don't drift from what works.
